name: Active Buzzer (5V)
desc: Beeps at one fixed pitch as soon as it gets power. Super simple alarms and alerts: just turn a pin on or off.
variantNote: Active: has its own oscillator, so it only beeps one tone. Usually has a sticker on top and is sealed underneath.
note: Polarity matters: the longer leg (+) goes to the signal side.

name: Passive Buzzer
desc: A buzzer that can play any note you choose with tone(), so it can play melodies and game sounds.
variantNote: Passive: needs a tone signal. You can see the green circuit board underneath.

name: Small Speaker (8Ω, 0.5–3W)
desc: A real speaker for music and voices. Much better sound than a buzzer, but it always needs an amplifier.
note: Never connect a speaker straight to a board pin. Use an amplifier (PAM8403, MAX98357A) or a DFPlayer Mini.

name: PAM8403 Stereo Amp (2×3W)
desc: A small amplifier that makes audio loud enough for two speakers. Often comes with a volume knob.
note: Each speaker connects only to its own + and − outputs. Never connect a speaker − to GND: that can destroy the amp.

name: DFPlayer Mini MP3 Player
desc: Plays MP3 files from a microSD card and drives a small speaker by itself. Perfect for sound effects, voice lines and music boxes.
note: Use a microSD card of 32GB or less, formatted FAT32, with files named 0001.mp3, 0002.mp3 and so on.

warn.5: Put a 1kΩ resistor between the board's TX and the DFPlayer RX. Its pins are 3.3V, and this also removes buzzing noise.

name: MAX98357A I2S Amp (3W)
desc: A digital amplifier that turns an I2S audio stream straight into speaker sound. Clean audio for ESP32 and Pico projects.

warn.5: MAX98357A needs I2S audio, which the Uno, Nano, Mega and Leonardo don't have. Use an ESP32, ESP32-S3 or Pico.
